finalText:
Written to `CHANGELOG.md`. Summary of what I did and why:

- Went through all 380 commits in `commits.log` and the 127 rows in `merged-prs.tsv`.
- Everything tagged `chore(deps)`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `docs`, and `perf` is invisible to someone installing the package, so none of that made the cut.
- Of the 26 `fix(...)`/`feat(...)` commits in the raw log, only 11 have a matching entry in the merged-PR sheet — the other 15 reuse identical commit messages on different modules but were never actually merged (e.g. three "drop the duplicate header" commits on `core` that don't exist in the PR sheet, only the `http` one does). I treated the PR sheet as the authoritative record and built the notes from those 11.
- One of the 11 is a status-code change (401 vs 403 on expired tokens) that I flagged as Breaking since it'll trip up clients checking for `403` specifically — worth double-checking with whoever owns auth before you ship it under that heading, in case it was meant to be soft-launched instead.

Worth a quick sanity check on the `401`/`403` and empty-allowlist wording since I only had commit messages and diffstats to go on, not the actual diffs — no test infrastructure here to verify behavior directly.
